pairs: Navina has $30 more to her weekly budget than her younger sister and can afford to get one of the many online credit cards she likes. What do they each have to spend?

Let's call the amount Navina's sister has to spend x. Navina has $30 more, so she has to spend x + $30. Together, they have to spend $150, so we can set up the equation x + x + $30 = $150. Simplifying the equation, we get 2x + $30 = $150. Subtracting $30 from both sides, we get 2x = $120. Dividing both sides by 2, we get x = $60. So Navina's sister has to spend $60, and Navina has to spend $60 + $30 = $90. They can each spend \boxed{90} dollars.
